what_breaks: The email check is stricter than R-02. It refuses a domain part that starts or ends with a dot (for example 'a@b.' or 'a@.b'), but R-02 only asks for one @, text on both sides and a dot after the @. PLAN S2 Risks says 'nothing stricter'. tests/customers.test.js line 46 asserts that 'a@.' is refused, so the test locks in the stricter rule.
evidence: validateCustomer({name:'Ana', email:'a@b.'}): split gives local 'a' and domain 'b.'. domain.includes('.') is true, but domain.endsWith('.') is true, so isValidEmail returns false and errors.email is set. R-02 would accept this input.

what_breaks: Order text filter: the list shows order numbers as '#12' (orders-view.js line 81), but typing '#12' finds nothing, because the needle is compared with String(o.number) and '12' does not contain '#'. Matching is also a substring match, so '1' matches orders 1, 10, 11 and 21. R-10 says the text matches the order number.
evidence: filterOrders(state, {text:'#12'}) where an order has number 12: needle is '#12', '12'.includes('#12') is false, and the customer name has no '#', so the result is [] and the UI shows 'No orders match your filter.'

what_breaks: When stored data cannot be read (R-18), ctx.state falls back to an empty state, and the lists show 'No customers yet. Use "Add customer" to create the first one.' and 'No orders yet...' next to the error banner. The data exists but is unreadable, so the screen states a guessed value as certain and points to an action that is disabled.
evidence: app.js line 13 sets locked = true when load fails. Line 19 returns emptyState because store.current() is null. customers-view.js lines 57-58 see customers.length === 0 and render the 'No customers yet' empty-state text.

what_breaks: The shape check only checks types. It does not check that nextOrderNumber is greater than every stored order number, that customerId points to an existing customer, that IDs are unique, or that quantity and unitPriceCents are in range. Data edited by hand or damaged in these ways loads as valid. The app then reuses order numbers (breaks A-04), shows 'Unknown customer', or formats negative cents wrongly: formatEuros(-5) gives Math.floor(-0.05) = -1 and -5 % 100 = -5, so the text is '€-1.-5'.
evidence: Stored {version:1,nextOrderNumber:1,customers:[c1],orders:[{number:1,...}]} passes hasValidShape. The next addOrder assigns number 1 again (orders.js line 19). The app cannot reach this state through its own UI. To settle: add a store test that loads such data and expects ok:false.

what_breaks: The customer filter value in view.customerId is kept after that customer is deleted. Back on the Orders tab, select.value is set to an ID with no matching option, so the select shows blank while the filter still applies. The list then shows 'No orders match your filter.' even though orders exist.
evidence: Filter Orders by customer X (who has no orders), switch to Customers, delete X (allowed by R-05), then switch back to Orders. buildList sets select.value = X's id and no option matches. filterOrders uses customerId X and returns [], so buildResults line 73 shows the no-match message. To settle: run this sequence in the browser.

what_breaks: The load-time shape check tests only types, never the rules the domain enforces. Hand-edited or older data loads as valid even when it has an empty customer name, a negative or non-integer-range quantity, a negative or huge unitPriceCents, a date that is not a calendar date, or an email without an @. The app then shows these values as normal and puts them in totals.
evidence: hasValidShape (lines 25-29) calls allStrings and Number.isInteger only. The stored value {version:1,nextOrderNumber:1,customers:[{id:'c',name:'',email:'x',phone:''}],orders:[{id:'o',number:1,customerId:'c',date:'nope',lines:[{id:'l',description:'',quantity:-3,unitPriceCents:-5}]}]} passes every check, so load returns ok:true. Once loaded, formatEuros(-5) runs Math.floor(-0.05) = -1 and String(-5 % 100) = '-5', and renders '€-1.-5'. I traced this by reading the code. A node probe was refused by the scope guard, so I have not run it.

what_breaks: Stored references are trusted without a check. An order's customerId is never checked against the customers, and ids are not checked for duplicates. An orphan order shows as 'Unknown customer' and no customer filter can find it. With duplicate order ids, updateOrderDate, deleteOrder and the line edits match every copy at once.
evidence: isOrder only checks that customerId is a string. Nothing compares it with data.customers. orders.js deleteOrder filters by id and updateOrderDate maps by id, so two orders stored with id 'o' are both changed or both removed by one click. Probe: put an order with customerId 'ghost' in localStorage['invoice-app'], reload, and open the Orders tab.

what_breaks: nextOrderNumber is not checked against the order numbers already stored. If hand-edited or older data has nextOrderNumber at or below an existing number, the next new order gets a duplicate number. A-04 says order numbers are never reused.
evidence: hasValidShape only checks Number.isInteger(data.nextOrderNumber). With nextOrderNumber:1 and an existing order number:1, addOrder (orders.js line 19) creates a second order numbered 1. I traced this by reading the code. Probe: store that state, reload, and create an order.

what_breaks: window.localStorage is read at module top level, outside any try. When storage is disabled (for example the browser blocks all site data or cookies), the getter throws a SecurityError. The module never finishes loading, nothing renders under the header, and the banner never shows. The error appears only in the console. The store's own catch around getItem is never reached.
evidence: Line 5: const store = createStore(window.localStorage); has no try around it. store.load wraps only storage.getItem. Manual probe: in Chrome, block all site data for localhost, reload http://localhost:8000, and check whether the banner shows an error or the page is blank.

what_breaks: crypto.randomUUID only exists in secure contexts. If the app is opened from a non-localhost http address (for example a LAN IP), newId throws a TypeError inside the submit handler. Add customer, New order and Add line then do nothing, with no message on the page.
evidence: newId: () => crypto.randomUUID() is called before the domain call in customers-view.js line 158, orders-view.js line 123 and lines-view.js line 105, and none of these is guarded. Manual probe: serve with python3 -m http.server 8000 and open http://<LAN-IP>:8000, then add a customer.

what_breaks: Raw exception messages are shown in the banner. A JSON.parse SyntaxError message can include part of the stored text, and DOMException messages differ by browser. Everything goes through textContent, so nothing can run as markup. This is only an exposure of internals in the page.
evidence: readableError returns error.message. app.js showError sets banner.textContent, which is safe as text. Probe: set localStorage['invoice-app'] to '{bad' and reload to see the message text.

what_breaks: CI checks out ioanbitza/sdlc-kit at its default branch with no pinned ref or sha, then runs its gate.mjs. Any later change to that repository changes what CI runs and what it passes, without a change in this repository.
evidence: The step 'uses: actions/checkout@v4 with repository: ioanbitza/sdlc-kit, path: .sdlc-kit' has no 'ref:'. It is followed by 'run: node .sdlc-kit/tools/gate.mjs --strict'. Probe: check whether ADR-002 means the gate version to be fixed.

what_breaks: The email check is stricter than R-02. An email whose part after the @ starts or ends with a dot (for example 'a@.com' or 'a@b.com.') has one @, text on both sides and a dot after the @, yet it is refused with 'Enter an email like name@example.com'. No test pins this extra rule.
evidence: Code: `return local.length > 0 && domain.length > 0 && domain.includes('.') && !domain.startsWith('.') && !domain.endsWith('.');`. R-02: 'An email, when given, must contain one `@` with text on both sides and a dot in the part after it'. PLAN S2 Risks: 'the email rule is exactly the one in R-02 and nothing stricter.'

what_breaks: PLAN S7 step 4 is not done. The customer view lists the customer's orders as plain text (`el('td', `#${order.number}`)`), and app.js wires nothing to open an order from there. A user who opens a customer cannot reach any of their orders from that screen.
evidence: PLAN S7 step 4: '`app.js` wires the Orders tab and opening an order from the customer view.' src/ui/app.js holds only tab switching (lines 65-71). customers-view.js buildCustomerOrders has no button or handler on the rows. customers-view.js is not on S7's Files line, so S7 could not add one there.

what_breaks: The empty state for a customer with no orders gives no next action, although one exists: create an order for this customer. The order form also cannot be opened with this customer already chosen.
evidence: Code: `el('p', 'This customer has no orders yet.', { class: 'empty' })`. R-20: '... each show a short message saying so, with the next action where there is one.' Whether R-20 counts 'a customer's order list' as one of its listed states (no customers, no orders, no lines, no search results) can be read two ways.

what_breaks: The UI repeats the data model's empty state, which is already defined in src/storage/store.js emptyState(). When the load fails, the views render this object, so the customer list says 'No customers yet. Use "Add customer"...' while data that cannot be read is still stored.
evidence: app.js: `const emptyState = { version: 1, nextOrderNumber: 1, customers: [], orders: [] };` and `get state() { return store.current() ?? emptyState; }`. AGENTS.md: '`src/ui/` DOM rendering and events. No business rules here.' R-18 asks only that an error is shown and the data is not overwritten. Whether a 'no customers' message under the banner counts as wrong behaviour is a judgement call.

what_breaks: centsToInput converts cents to a euro text in the UI. The money rule for this conversion belongs in src/domain/money.js.
evidence: lines-view.js: `return `${Math.floor(cents / 100)}.${String(cents % 100).padStart(2, '0')}`;`. PLAN shared design: 'Money is integer cents everywhere. Text becomes cents only in `src/domain/money.js`.' AGENTS.md: 'src/ui/ ... No business rules here.' This converts cents to text, not text to cents, so whether the plan line covers it is open.

what_breaks: The general DOM helpers `el` and `button` are exported from lines-view.js and imported by orders-view.js, while customers-view.js keeps its own copy. Shared helpers end up in an unrelated view module.
evidence: orders-view.js: `import { el, button, renderLines } from './lines-view.js';`. customers-view.js lines 9-20 define the same el and button again. AGENTS.md rule 7: 'Small functions, plain names, no speculative abstractions or "utils" dumping grounds.'

what_breaks: A UI module references localStorage directly to inject it into the store.
evidence: app.js: `const store = createStore(window.localStorage);`. AGENTS.md: '`src/storage/` the only code that touches localStorage.' The PLAN shared design asks for injection: 'The store in `src/storage/` gets the storage object injected (`createStore(storage)`)'. Whether passing the reference counts as touching localStorage is for the human to decide.

what_breaks: Commit b00627a ticks all 23 manual checks at once under the message 'Manual checks', which is not in the `S<n>: ... (R-xx)` form. Nothing in the repository shows which checks a human actually ran.
evidence: git log: 'b00627a Bita Ioan | Manual checks', and that diff changes every line from '- [ ]' to '- [x]'. AGENTS.md rule 8: 'One commit per finished slice: `S<n>: <what changed> (R-xx, R-yy)`.' ADR-002: 'The human ... ticks only the manual checks they ran'. Authorship alone cannot settle whether a human or an agent ran them.

what_breaks: Commit 6ac3155 adds the new folders .github/workflows/ and .githooks/, which are not in the AGENTS.md structure and not on any plan slice.
evidence: AGENTS.md rule 5: 'No new dependencies and no folders outside the structure above.' ADR-001 'Not decided here: Configuration files at the repository root'. ADR-002 does cover them: 'One gate script ... runs in the Claude hooks, in the git hooks and in CI.' So these may be human-decided kit files rather than slice output.
